title: Grateful Dead Live at Worcester Polytechnic Institute on 1970-05-09
lineage: SBD > MR > ? > DAT > CDR > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Muddy, hissy audience recording of a brief acoustic set – Jerry shines but the sound and length hold it back.
ai_review.review: The tape captures a short, mostly‑acoustic show that many fans recall fondly for Jerry Garcia’s clear folk voice and a strong rendition of Black Peter. Unfortunately the source is an old cassette/mic feed that sounds saturated, hissy and often muddy, making the listening experience uneven. While the performance itself has moments of charm, the poor recording quality and truncated set keep it from being a must‑hear.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers criticize the audio (poor audience cassette) while a minority praise Jerry’s acoustic playing; weighting show (≈3) and recording (≈2) yields an overall low‑mid rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Saturated, hissy, muddy tape with occasional overload; appears to be a microphone/cassette capture rather than a true soundboard feed. Short duration and frequent distortion noted.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A brief acoustic set (Monkey, Engineer, Black Peter, Deep Ellum Blues, etc.) followed by a long break before an electric portion that isn’t captured on this tape. The acoustic segment is praised for its intimacy but criticized for being short and occasionally tired.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for pure, strong folk‑style vocals and guitar work; highlighted as a standout element of the set.
